questions.question: You see a yellow circle with the letters “MB” inside it painted on the road surface. What does this marking mean?

options.text: Only motorbikes may park here.
Only medical buses may stop here.
Only minibus taxis may stop or park here.
This is a mandatory bus lane.

questions.question: A parking bay is marked with the letter “F”. Who may park there?

options.text: Fire trucks
Farmers’ vehicles
Visitors for Funeral purposes
Disabled drivers

questions.question: What does a yellow criss-cross (box junction) painted on the road mean?

options.text: You may stop in the area if traffic is heavy.
You may stop only if you are turning right.
You are not allowed to stop in that area.
The area is reserved for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: A parking bay has the wheelchair symbol painted in it. Who may park there?

options.text: Anyone if the bay is empty
Only vehicles displaying a disabled permit
Elderly people only
Medical staff

questions.question: What does a road sign showing “Arrestor Bed Ahead” mean?

options.text: A place for police roadblocks.
A safe area for vehicles to turn around.
A sand/gravel bed for vehicles with brake failure.
A resting area for trucks.

questions.question: A parking bay marked with the letter “R” is reserved for:

options.text: Residents
Rickshaws
Rental cars
Roadworthy testing

questions.explanation: The video says 'R' bays are reserved for rickshaws only. Note: in the NaTIS manual the letter 'R' on a sign means the area is reserved, and the symbol with it shows for whom (motor cars, taxis, buses, etc.). Rickshaw reservation (R318/R318-P) shows a rickshaw symbol, so a plain 'R' does not by itself mean rickshaws.
questions.manualRef: NaTIS Learner Driver Manual – Road Traffic Signs §3.4 Reservation signs (p.17)

questions.question: What does a solid line separating two lanes of opposite-direction traffic mean?

options.text: You may overtake if the road ahead is clear.
You may cross the line only to turn into a driveway.
You are not allowed to cross the line.
You may cross the line during the day only.

questions.question: You see tram tracks or a “TRAM” road marking on the lane you are driving in. What must you do?

options.text: You may drive freely as long as no tram is near.
Give way to trams and do not drive on the tracks unless allowed.
Stop immediately and wait for the tram to pass.
Overtake the tram if it is moving slowly.

questions.question: What does a red line painted along the edge of the road mean?

options.text: You may stop to load or unload passengers only.
You may stop briefly if no traffic is coming.
You are not allowed to stop at all, except for emergencies.
You may park there at night only.

questions.question: What does a block style pedestrian crossing (zebra stripes) painted across the road mean?

options.text: Only school children may cross there.
Vehicles have right of way, pedestrians must wait.
Pedestrians have right of way, vehicles must stop if someone is crossing.
Only cyclists may use it.
